# terminal column wrapping

A command-line report tool lays text out in terminal columns, where CJK characters and emoji occupy two cells and combining marks none.

This repository holds the Rust implementation (`src/lib.rs`). It is being ported to Python; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

Terminal columns. Every Unicode code point has a **display width**:

* `0` for the combining marks U+0300..U+036F,
* `2` for the "wide" code points in these ranges (inclusive): U+1100..U+115F, U+2E80..U+303E, U+3041..U+33FF,
  U+3400..U+4DBF, U+4E00..U+9FFF, U+A000..U+A4CF, U+AC00..U+D7A3, U+F900..U+FAFF, U+FE30..U+FE4F, U+FF00..U+FF60,
  U+FFE0..U+FFE6, U+1F300..U+1F64F, U+1F900..U+1F9FF, U+20000..U+2FFFD, U+30000..U+3FFFD,
* `1` for everything else.

A text is a sequence of code points (no lone surrogates). The only separator is the space U+0020; `\n` ends a paragraph.

* `display_width(text)` is the sum of the widths of its code points.
* `clip(text, width)` is the longest prefix of whole code points whose cumulative width stays `<= width`; scanning stops
  at the first code point that does not fit. `width < 0` is an error.
* `pad_to(text, width)` appends spaces until the display width reaches `width`; a text that is already as wide or wider is
  returned unchanged.
* `wrap(text, width)` returns lines. `width < 2` is an error. Split the text on `\n`; every paragraph is wrapped on its own and an
  empty paragraph (no words) gives one empty line `""`. Inside a paragraph, words are the maximal runs of non-space
  code points (runs of spaces collapse, leading and trailing spaces vanish). Words are added greedily to the current
  line, separated by one space, as long as the line's display width stays `<= width`. A word whose own display width
  exceeds `width` is broken: the current line (if any) is closed first, then the word is cut with repeated `clip`
  calls into pieces; every full piece is a line and the final remainder (which fits) becomes the current line, so
  following words can join it. A closed line is never empty except for the empty-paragraph case.

## Functions

* `display_width(text)` -> `int`. (`text`: str)
* `clip(text, width)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `width`: int)
* `pad_to(text, width)` -> `str`. (`text`: str, `width`: int)
* `wrap(text, width)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `width`: int)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

# terminal column wrapping

A command-line report tool lays text out in terminal columns, where CJK characters and emoji occupy two cells and combining marks none.

This repository holds the Python implementation (`col_wrap.py`). It is being ported to TypeScript; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

Terminal columns. Every Unicode code point has a **display width**:

* `0` for the combining marks U+0300..U+036F,
* `2` for the "wide" code points in these ranges (inclusive): U+1100..U+115F, U+2E80..U+303E, U+3041..U+33FF,
  U+3400..U+4DBF, U+4E00..U+9FFF, U+A000..U+A4CF, U+AC00..U+D7A3, U+F900..U+FAFF, U+FE30..U+FE4F, U+FF00..U+FF60,
  U+FFE0..U+FFE6, U+1F300..U+1F64F, U+1F900..U+1F9FF, U+20000..U+2FFFD, U+30000..U+3FFFD,
* `1` for everything else.

A text is a sequence of code points (no lone surrogates). The only separator is the space U+0020; `\n` ends a paragraph.

* `display_width(text)` is the sum of the widths of its code points.
* `clip(text, width)` is the longest prefix of whole code points whose cumulative width stays `<= width`; scanning stops
  at the first code point that does not fit. `width < 0` is an error.
* `pad_to(text, width)` appends spaces until the display width reaches `width`; a text that is already as wide or wider is
  returned unchanged.
* `wrap(text, width)` returns lines. `width < 2` is an error. Split the text on `\n`; every paragraph is wrapped on its own and an
  empty paragraph (no words) gives one empty line `""`. Inside a paragraph, words are the maximal runs of non-space
  code points (runs of spaces collapse, leading and trailing spaces vanish). Words are added greedily to the current
  line, separated by one space, as long as the line's display width stays `<= width`. A word whose own display width
  exceeds `width` is broken: the current line (if any) is closed first, then the word is cut with repeated `clip`
  calls into pieces; every full piece is a line and the final remainder (which fits) becomes the current line, so
  following words can join it. A closed line is never empty except for the empty-paragraph case.

## Functions

* `display_width(text)` -> `int`. (`text`: str)
* `clip(text, width)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `width`: int)
* `pad_to(text, width)` -> `str`. (`text`: str, `width`: int)
* `wrap(text, width)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `width`: int)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

# terminal column wrapping

A command-line report tool lays text out in terminal columns, where CJK characters and emoji occupy two cells and combining marks none.

This repository holds the TypeScript implementation (`src/col_wrap.ts`). It is being ported to Rust; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

Terminal columns. Every Unicode code point has a **display width**:

* `0` for the combining marks U+0300..U+036F,
* `2` for the "wide" code points in these ranges (inclusive): U+1100..U+115F, U+2E80..U+303E, U+3041..U+33FF,
  U+3400..U+4DBF, U+4E00..U+9FFF, U+A000..U+A4CF, U+AC00..U+D7A3, U+F900..U+FAFF, U+FE30..U+FE4F, U+FF00..U+FF60,
  U+FFE0..U+FFE6, U+1F300..U+1F64F, U+1F900..U+1F9FF, U+20000..U+2FFFD, U+30000..U+3FFFD,
* `1` for everything else.

A text is a sequence of code points (no lone surrogates). The only separator is the space U+0020; `\n` ends a paragraph.

* `display_width(text)` is the sum of the widths of its code points.
* `clip(text, width)` is the longest prefix of whole code points whose cumulative width stays `<= width`; scanning stops
  at the first code point that does not fit. `width < 0` is an error.
* `pad_to(text, width)` appends spaces until the display width reaches `width`; a text that is already as wide or wider is
  returned unchanged.
* `wrap(text, width)` returns lines. `width < 2` is an error. Split the text on `\n`; every paragraph is wrapped on its own and an
  empty paragraph (no words) gives one empty line `""`. Inside a paragraph, words are the maximal runs of non-space
  code points (runs of spaces collapse, leading and trailing spaces vanish). Words are added greedily to the current
  line, separated by one space, as long as the line's display width stays `<= width`. A word whose own display width
  exceeds `width` is broken: the current line (if any) is closed first, then the word is cut with repeated `clip`
  calls into pieces; every full piece is a line and the final remainder (which fits) becomes the current line, so
  following words can join it. A closed line is never empty except for the empty-paragraph case.

## Functions

* `display_width(text)` -> `int`. (`text`: str)
* `clip(text, width)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `width`: int)
* `pad_to(text, width)` -> `str`. (`text`: str, `width`: int)
* `wrap(text, width)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `width`: int)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## TypeScript (source)

```ts
export function displayWidth(text: string): number
export function clip(text: string, width: number): string
export function padTo(text: string, width: number): string
export function wrap(text: string, width: number): string[]
```

## Rust (target)

The Rust API already exists as stubs (every function fails at run time); replace the bodies.

Crate `col_wrap`: everything is reachable from `src/lib.rs` (extra modules are fine; re-export them). Failure is an `Err(_)` (the error type is yours); never panic on bad input. No dependencies.

```rust
pub fn display_width(text: &str) -> i64
pub fn clip(text: &str, width: i64) -> Result<String, E>
pub fn pad_to(text: &str, width: i64) -> String
pub fn wrap(text: &str, width: i64) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
```

## Checking

`tests/vectors.rs` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the Rust API; run `cargo test --offline`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.

# terminal column wrapping

A command-line report tool lays text out in terminal columns, where CJK characters and emoji occupy two cells and combining marks none.

This repository holds the Rust implementation (`src/lib.rs`). It is being ported to TypeScript; the port must behave exactly like the specification below, including for malformed input.

## Behaviour

Terminal columns. Every Unicode code point has a **display width**:

* `0` for the combining marks U+0300..U+036F,
* `2` for the "wide" code points in these ranges (inclusive): U+1100..U+115F, U+2E80..U+303E, U+3041..U+33FF,
  U+3400..U+4DBF, U+4E00..U+9FFF, U+A000..U+A4CF, U+AC00..U+D7A3, U+F900..U+FAFF, U+FE30..U+FE4F, U+FF00..U+FF60,
  U+FFE0..U+FFE6, U+1F300..U+1F64F, U+1F900..U+1F9FF, U+20000..U+2FFFD, U+30000..U+3FFFD,
* `1` for everything else.

A text is a sequence of code points (no lone surrogates). The only separator is the space U+0020; `\n` ends a paragraph.

* `display_width(text)` is the sum of the widths of its code points.
* `clip(text, width)` is the longest prefix of whole code points whose cumulative width stays `<= width`; scanning stops
  at the first code point that does not fit. `width < 0` is an error.
* `pad_to(text, width)` appends spaces until the display width reaches `width`; a text that is already as wide or wider is
  returned unchanged.
* `wrap(text, width)` returns lines. `width < 2` is an error. Split the text on `\n`; every paragraph is wrapped on its own and an
  empty paragraph (no words) gives one empty line `""`. Inside a paragraph, words are the maximal runs of non-space
  code points (runs of spaces collapse, leading and trailing spaces vanish). Words are added greedily to the current
  line, separated by one space, as long as the line's display width stays `<= width`. A word whose own display width
  exceeds `width` is broken: the current line (if any) is closed first, then the word is cut with repeated `clip`
  calls into pieces; every full piece is a line and the final remainder (which fits) becomes the current line, so
  following words can join it. A closed line is never empty except for the empty-paragraph case.

## Functions

* `display_width(text)` -> `int`. (`text`: str)
* `clip(text, width)` -> `str`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `width`: int)
* `pad_to(text, width)` -> `str`. (`text`: str, `width`: int)
* `wrap(text, width)` -> `list<str>`. Fails on invalid input. (`text`: str, `width`: int)

Types: `int` is a signed 64-bit integer and every value in the test vectors is within +-2^53; `str` is Unicode text; `list<T>` is an ordered sequence.

## Rust (source)

```rust
pub fn display_width(text: &str) -> i64
pub fn clip(text: &str, width: i64) -> Result<String, E>
pub fn pad_to(text: &str, width: i64) -> String
pub fn wrap(text: &str, width: i64) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>
```

## TypeScript (target)

The TypeScript API already exists as stubs (every function fails at run time); replace the bodies.

Module `src/col_wrap.ts` with one `export function` per function. The test run includes `tsc -p .` with `strict` enabled, so the code must type-check. Numbers are `number`; `u32` values are non-negative integers below 2^32. Failure is signalled by throwing an exception. An absent `opt` value is `null`.

```ts
export function displayWidth(text: string): number
export function clip(text: string, width: number): string
export function padTo(text: string, width: number): string
export function wrap(text: string, width: number): string[]
```

## Checking

`test/vectors.test.ts` reads the vector file `vectors/examples.json` (a small sample) and calls the TypeScript API; run `tsc -p . && node --test build/test/*.test.js`. The same harness is used with a much larger vector file when the port is graded, so passing the examples only is not enough. The harness files and `vectors/examples.json` must not be edited.
